papers.title: The pharmacological potential and metabolic risks of Xiaojin Pill in sorafenib-resistant papillary thyroid carcinoma: an integrated network analysis.
papers.abstract: Sorafenib resistance limits the efficacy of treatments for advanced papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC). The antitumor potential of Xiaojin Pill (XJP) has been demonstrated, yet its mechanisms potentially implicated in sorafenib resistance and combinational toxicological risks remain unclear. This study aimed to examine the molecular mechanisms through which XJP may act on signaling pathways implicated in sorafenib resistance, and to assess its combinational toxicological risks during co-administration with sorafenib.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated network analysis to predict how the traditional Chinese medicine Xiaojin Pill might act on signaling pathways involved in sorafenib resistance in papillary thyroid carcinoma, and to assess toxicological risks of combining it with sorafenib. The work is largely computational and hypothesis-generating, identifying candidate mechanisms and potential safety concerns rather than providing experimental validation.

papers.title: Discovery of benzimidazole-based selective α-glucosidase inhibitors with an uncompetitive mode of action: synthesis, biological assays and computational studies.
papers.abstract: A series of thirteen 1-(benzyloxy)-2-phenyl-1H-benzo[d]imidazole derivatives was designed, synthesized, and evaluated as α-glucosidase inhibitors. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that the presence of a chlorine atom at the C-6 position of the benzimidazole core, combined with suitable substituents on the pendant aromatic rings, was associated with relevant α-glucosidase inhibitory activity. Among the series, compounds 6 and 13 emerged as the most potent derivatives showing IC50 values of 32.35 μM and 15.70 μM, respectively, and greater potency than acarbose (IC50 = 139 μM) un
papers.summary: The authors synthesized thirteen benzimidazole derivatives and tested them as α-glucosidase inhibitors, finding that compounds 6 and 13 inhibit the enzyme more potently than the standard drug acarbose (IC50 values of 32.35 μM and 15.70 μM vs 139 μM). Computational studies indicate these compounds act through an uncompetitive mechanism, and structure-activity analysis highlights a C-6 chlorine substituent as important for activity.

papers.title: Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints.
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. In particular, there are cases where experimental data, such as distances between residue pairs in interacting proteins are available, yet existing prediction methods fail t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Distance-AF Multimer is a new computational pipeline that incorporates user-defined distance constraints into protein complex structure prediction, addressing cases where standard methods like AlphaFold-Multimer fail to assemble complexes correctly despite available experimental distance data. The approach uses a multi-step workflow to guide modeling with these constraints, improving accuracy for challenging complexes.

papers.title: Free-Energy and Molecular Dynamics Analysis of Ser195 and Thr195 Rotameric States in Thrombin.
papers.abstract: Ser195 is highly conserved as the catalytic nucleophile in trypsin-like serine proteases, yet the molecular basis for the strong preference for serine over the chemically similar threonine residue remains unclear. Here, we used well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond-long molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to characterize the conformational energetics of S195 and T195 in thrombin. Well-tempered metadynamics revealed distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes in both the apo and the ligand-bound systems. In the apo state, S195 preferentially occupied a lower-angle rotameric state, while T195
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study uses well-tempered metadynamics and microsecond molecular dynamics simulations to compare the conformational energetics of serine versus threonine at position 195 in thrombin, a site where serine is strongly conserved across trypsin-like serine proteases. The authors find that S195 and T195 occupy distinct rotameric free-energy landscapes in both apo and ligand-bound states, with S195 favoring a lower-angle rotamer in the apo state. The work offers a molecular explanation for why serine is preferred over the chemically similar threonine at the catalytic nucleophile position.

papers.title: Edge-Aware Graph Attention Networks for Interpreting Biophysical Mechanisms from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Graph attention networks (GATs) are emerging as powerful aritficial intelligence (AI) tools for learning biomolecular dynamics, yet extracting mechanistic insight from learned attention remains challenging. Here, we present an interpretable AI approach that combines molecular dynamics prediction with mechanistic interpretation through attention-derived communication networks. We develop three edge-aware GAT models - Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, and Edge-Gated - that differ in how edge information is incorporated during message passing. Relative to a standard GAT, our edge-aware models impr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint introduces three edge-aware graph attention network variants (Edge-Conditioned, Edge-Injected, Edge-Gated) for learning biomolecular dynamics from molecular dynamics simulations, differing in how edge features are incorporated during message passing. The authors show these models improve prediction relative to a standard GAT and, importantly, use the learned attention weights to derive 'communication networks' that offer mechanistic interpretation of biophysical processes. The work aims to bridge predictive AI with interpretable mechanistic insight from MD data.

papers.title: A computational-experimental strategy identifies K-7174 against African swine fever.
papers.abstract: African swine fever (ASF), caused by the African swine fever virus (ASFV), poses a catastrophic threat to global swine production due to the absence of effective vaccines or therapeutics. Targeting the virally encoded RNA polymerase (RNAP), which is essential for viral transcription, offers a promising antiviral strategy. Capitalizing on our previously resolved high-resolution structure of ASFV RNAP, we conducted a rigorous structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries (T001 and LF1000) to identify selective inhibitors. From 100 candidates validated in vitro, nine compounds ident
papers.summary: The authors used the high-resolution structure of the African swine fever virus RNA polymerase to perform structure-based virtual screening of two compound libraries, identifying nine candidate inhibitors from 100 in vitro-validated compounds. One compound, K-7174, emerged as a promising antiviral hit against ASF, demonstrating a computational-experimental pipeline for antiviral discovery.

papers.title: Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.
papers.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling via its receptor (IL-6R) is a central driver of inflammation and immune-related diseases. Although monoclonal antibodies targeting this pathway are clinically effective, their limitations, including high costs and parenteral administration, create an urgent need for orally available small-molecule inhibitors. However, targeting the extensive protein‒protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R remains a significant challenge.
papers.summary: This study identifies novel small-molecule binders that target different conformational states of the IL-6 receptor, aiming to block IL-6 signaling as an alternative to antibody-based therapies. By focusing on the challenging protein–protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R, the work opens a potential route to orally available inhibitors for inflammatory and immune-related diseases.

papers.title: LHCGR disruption and downregulation by bisphenol PH impairs ovarian function and establishes a prioritization framework for endocrine disruptors.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol analogs (BPs) are recognized endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) significantly threaten ovarian health; however, the characterization of high-risk compounds, molecular initiating events (MIEs), and toxicity mechanisms associated with specific diseases remains insufficient.
papers.summary: This study shows that the bisphenol analog bisphenol PH disrupts ovarian function by downregulating the LHCGR receptor, and the authors use this finding to build a framework for ranking endocrine-disrupting chemicals by risk. The work links a specific molecular initiating event to ovarian toxicity and offers a general approach for prioritizing high-risk environmental chemicals.

papers.title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.
papers.abstract: Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning-based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog-aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence-based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning-based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize
papers.summary: EZpred is a deep learning method that improves enzyme function prediction (EC number assignment) by incorporating features from unlabeled sequence homologs, analogous to how homolog-aware structure prediction models like AlphaFold outperform single-sequence methods. This demonstrates that leveraging evolutionary information from homologous sequences, even without function labels, boosts prediction accuracy.

papers.title: Superionic Al─O─H Compounds With Unconventional Stoichiometries Under Extreme Planetary Conditions.
papers.abstract: Extreme pressure and temperature induce novel chemical behaviors, including unconventional stoichiometries and superionic states. Here, by combining crystal structure prediction with first-principles calculations, we identify two unconventional stoichiometries in the ternary Al─O─H system, AlOH and AlH3O4, which lie on the convex hull at 300 GPa. Representative formation reactions become thermodynamically stable above 65 and 245 GPa after including ZPE, respectively. Both compounds are wide-gap insulators and AlH3O4 exhibits pronounced site-dependent charge differentiation between inequivalent
papers.summary: Using crystal structure prediction and first-principles calculations, the authors identify two previously unknown Al-O-H compounds (AlOH and AlH3O4) with unconventional stoichiometries that are thermodynamically stable at extreme pressures (above 65 and 245 GPa, respectively). Both are wide-gap insulators, and AlH3O4 shows strong site-dependent charge differentiation. These findings expand the known chemistry of ternary hydrous systems under planetary interior conditions.

papers.title: Thiophen-2-ylsulfonyl indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazones as selective prostate cancer agents: biological profiling and molecular targeting studies.
papers.abstract: A series of thiophen-2-ylsulfonyl indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazone derivatives 5a-5t was synthesized and evaluated for anticancer activity using biological and computational methods. The cytotoxic activity of these compounds was tested on A549, LNCaP, and HUVEC cell lines utilizing the MTT assay, with sorafenib used as a control drug. The activity of the derivatives was shown to be cell line- and substituent-dependent, with the highest cytotoxicity against LNCaP cells. Compound 5d, bearing a 2,3-dichlorophenyl group, was the most potent derivative against LNCaP cells (IC50 = 2.50 µM; SI
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a series of thiophen-2-ylsulfonyl indole-3-carbaldehyde thiosemicarbazone derivatives and screened them for anticancer activity against lung (A549), prostate (LNCaP), and normal endothelial (HUVEC) cell lines. Compound 5d, featuring a 2,3-dichlorophenyl substituent, showed the most potent and selective cytotoxicity against prostate cancer cells (IC50 = 2.50 µM). Computational docking studies suggest the compounds act through a specific molecular target, supporting further development as prostate cancer therapeutics.

papers.title: Data-Driven Design of Biofunctional Molecularly Imprinted Polymers for Precision Diagnostics.
papers.abstract: Conventional imprinted receptors design is laborious and reliant on trial-and-error experimentation. To overcome existing challenges, this study integrates molecular mechanics/molecular dynamics (MM/MD) and machine learning (ML) to design molecularly imprinted polymer nanoparticles (nanoMIPs), aiming to uncover synergies and gaps between physics-informed and data-driven approaches. By systematically comparing and experimentally evaluating MM/MD formulations with ML-predicted recipes, we establish a multimodal framework for cross-validation, method selection, and accelerated development of biom
papers.summary: This study combines molecular mechanics/molecular dynamics simulations with machine learning to design molecularly imprinted polymer nanoparticles (nanoMIPs) for diagnostic applications, replacing laborious trial-and-error approaches. The authors systematically compare physics-informed and data-driven design strategies, experimentally validating both and establishing a multimodal framework for cross-validation and accelerated development of biofunctional imprinted receptors.

papers.title: Azobenzene-mediated reversible conformational switching in 9,9'-bifluorenylidene-based molecular machines.
papers.abstract: Intrinsically dynamic molecules offer attractive building blocks for molecular machines, yet controlling their conformational motion with external stimuli remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report Azo-BF-Azo, a visible-light-driven molecular machine in which an intrinsically dynamic 9,9'-bifluorenylidene (BF) core is coupled to two photoswitchable tetra-ortho-fluorinated azobenzene (Azo) units that act as molecular actuators. By using variable-temperature NMR spectroscopy and UV-vis spectroscopy, together with computational studies, we demonstrate that irradiation at 525 nm induces Azo
papers.summary: The authors designed a molecular machine (Azo-BF-Azo) that combines a flexible 9,9'-bifluorenylidene core with two fluorinated azobenzene photoswitches acting as actuators. Using variable-temperature NMR, UV-vis spectroscopy, and computation, they show that 525 nm light drives reversible conformational switching of the molecule. This demonstrates external light control over intrinsic molecular motion in a synthetic system.

papers.title: Graphics processing unit-accelerated quantum simulation for molecular biology and drug discovery: algorithms, platforms, and emerging applications.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence has intensified the need for methods that describe molecular systems with quantum-mechanical accuracy. Gate-based quantum computing offers a principled framework for simulating electronic structure, molecular interactions, and biological processes at a fidelity inaccessible to classical force fields or density functional theory alone, yet scarce, noisy hardware limits direct experimentation. Graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated quantum simulation has emerged as a practical bridge, allowing quantum algorithms to be developed, validated, and benchmarked on classical
papers.summary: This review surveys how GPUs are being used to simulate quantum computers, enabling researchers to develop and test quantum algorithms for molecular biology and drug discovery without needing actual quantum hardware. It covers the algorithms, software platforms, and emerging applications that make GPU-accelerated quantum simulation a practical bridge between classical computing and future quantum advantage in the life sciences.

papers.title: Psychotropic Drug GST Interactions: In Vitro Inhibition, Molecular Docking, and Translational Potential in Cancer Therapy.
papers.abstract: Psychotropic drugs are widely used to treat mental disorders, but they also influence cellular pathways linked to cancer. One key enzyme, Glutathione S-transferase (GST), is involved in detoxification and drug resistance in tumors, making it a potential target in cancer therapy. This study examined the effects of selected psychotropic agents aripiprazole, fluoxetine hydrochloride, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate on GST activity derived from equine liver. Enzyme kinetics were assessed in vitro using 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (CDNB) as the substrate and ethacrynic acid (Kᵢ = 4.7
papers.journal: Journal of biochemical and molecular toxicology
papers.summary: This study tested five psychotropic drugs (aripiprazole, fluoxetine, risperidone, haloperidol, and sodium valproate) for their ability to inhibit glutathione S-transferase (GST), an enzyme involved in detoxification and tumor drug resistance, using equine liver enzyme and CDNB as substrate. The authors combined in vitro enzyme kinetics with molecular docking to characterize inhibition and assess translational potential for cancer therapy. The work suggests these drugs may modulate GST activity, hinting at possible repurposing opportunities, though the use of equine liver enzyme and preliminary docking limits direct clinical relevance.

papers.title: Molecular force gates regulate mechanical transmission across the nuclear envelope.
papers.abstract: The LINC (linker of nucleoskeleton and cytoskeleton) complex is a central mechanotransductive apparatus that physically couples cytoskeletal forces to the nuclear interior, thereby regulating nuclear architecture, chromatin organization, and downstream signaling. Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we identify and characterize 'force gates' within the LINC complex - structural interactions that maintain mechanical connectivity under load. By introducing targeted mutations into the KASH peptide and SUN protein, we provide computational evidence that a key disulfide bond (SUN2 Cys563
papers.summary: Using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, the authors identify 'force gates' within the LINC complex—specific structural interactions that keep the cytoskeleton mechanically coupled to the nuclear interior under load. Targeted mutations in the KASH peptide and SUN2 protein suggest that a key disulfide bond (SUN2 Cys563) is critical for maintaining this mechanical connectivity. The work offers a molecular-level explanation for how force is transmitted across the nuclear envelope.

papers.title: Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.
papers.abstract: 4-Nonylphenol (4-NP) is a persistent endocrine-disrupting chemical, but its role in allergic rhinitis (AR) remains poorly understood. The study here integrated human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and experimental validation to investigate the mechanisms underlying 4-NP-aggravated AR. Network analysis identified four shared candidates, e.g., CDKN1A, SKIL, IFNG, and B4GALT1. In an independent cohort, IFNG and SKIL were down-regulated in AR, whereas CDKN1A was increased. Single-cell analysis showed that IFNG was mainly expressed in T-cells. Molecul
papers.summary: This study integrates human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, and molecular modeling to show that the endocrine disruptor 4-nonylphenol worsens allergic rhinitis by impairing IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation. Key shared genes (IFNG, SKIL, CDKN1A, B4GALT1) were identified, with IFNG and SKIL down-regulated and CDKN1A up-regulated in AR patients, and IFNG expression localized mainly to T-cells.

papers.title: Comprehensive structure-based virtual screening of natural products enabling the discovery of new activators of SIRT1.
papers.abstract: Sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), a class III histone deacetylase, regulates key signaling pathways associated with health and longevity. Age-related decline in SIRT1 contributes to metabolic, inflammatory, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative diseases. Although SIRT1-activating compounds (STACs) represent a promising therapeutic strategy, currently available activators show limited potency. This study aimed to identify novel natural SIRT1 activators using hierarchical virtual screening.
papers.summary: This study used hierarchical structure-based virtual screening to search natural product libraries for new SIRT1 activators, motivated by the limited potency of existing SIRT1-activating compounds. The approach identified candidate natural compounds with potential to activate SIRT1, a key regulator of aging-related metabolic, inflammatory, cardiovascular, and neurodegenerative pathways. The work provides a starting point for developing more potent natural SIRT1 activators.

papers.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
papers.abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple proba
papers.summary: The authors show that AlphaFold2's predicted residue-residue distance distributions (distograms) contain information about multiple protein conformations, even when a single structure is output. By analyzing these distributions, they demonstrate that alternative conformations of a known protein structure can be predicted from a standard AF2 run without manipulating the MSA. This suggests that multi-state structural information is latent in AF2 predictions and can be extracted to model conformational heterogeneity.

papers.title: Structure-Based Discovery of Coumarin-Triazole Derivatives Targeting the Conserved QGDNQ Motif of Chandipura RdRp.
papers.abstract: Chandipura virus (CHPV) is a recently discovered neurotropic virus associated with severe encephalitis in children and for which there is currently no specific antiviral treatment. The viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) is an attractive antiviral target because of its essential role in viral RNA synthesis and the presence of conserved catalytic motifs required for polymerase function. In this study, a structure-based computational approach was employed to investigate coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors targeting the conserved QGDNQ motif-containing region of CHPV RdRp.
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based computational docking to screen coumarin-triazole derivatives as potential inhibitors of the Chandipura virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, targeting its conserved QGDNQ catalytic motif. The work identifies candidate compounds in silico for a virus that currently lacks any approved antiviral treatment. Findings are preliminary and would require experimental validation to confirm antiviral activity.

papers.title: Targeting IL-1R1 and androgen receptor using natural compounds from Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum: an in silico and in vitro study.
papers.abstract: Lung and prostate cancers remain leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, driven by inflammation-mediated tumour progression and hormone-dependent signalling. IL-1R1 promotes chronic inflammation, metastasis, and tumour survival, while androgen receptor (AR) signalling is a central driver of prostate cancer growth. Simultaneous targeting of inflammatory and androgenic pathways represents a promising strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance.
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and in vitro assays to identify natural compounds from two medicinal plants (Aconitum heterophyllum and Podophyllum hexandrum) that can simultaneously inhibit IL-1R1 (an inflammation receptor) and the androgen receptor, two targets implicated in lung and prostate cancer. The authors propose dual targeting of inflammatory and hormone signaling as a strategy to overcome therapeutic resistance, though the abstract does not report specific compound identities or potency data.

papers.title: Integrated network toxicology and experimental validation identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between pyrethroid exposure and keloid.
papers.abstract: Keloids are fibroproliferative skin lesions characterized by excessive extracellular matrix deposition. The potential molecular links between pyrethroid exposure and keloid-associated alterations remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology combined with experimental validation to identify VCAM1 as a candidate molecular link between exposure to pyrethroid pesticides and keloid formation. The authors integrate toxicogenomic and keloid-associated gene networks to prioritize VCAM1, then validate its involvement experimentally. The work suggests a possible environmental exposure contribution to keloid pathogenesis, though the evidence is preliminary.

papers.title: N-glycoproteomic profiling reveals aberrant ITGB1 glycosylation in hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia.
papers.abstract: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) is a prevalent chronic lung disease in preterm infants, characterized by arrested alveolarization. Extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling and receptor signaling are critical for alveolarization and are strictly regulated by protein N-glycosylation. However, the specific role of the vital post-translational modification in BPD pathogenesis remains unexplored. The present research aims to delineate a N-glycoproteomic landscape and elucidate the glycosylation-associated pathogenic mechanisms in a murine BPD model.
papers.summary: This study profiles the N-glycoproteome in a mouse model of hyperoxia-induced bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD), a chronic lung disease of preterm infants marked by arrested alveolarization. The authors identify aberrant N-glycosylation of integrin beta-1 (ITGB1), suggesting a link between glycosylation-dependent ECM-receptor signaling and impaired lung development. The work provides a first N-glycoproteomic landscape for BPD and nominates ITGB1 glycosylation as a candidate pathogenic mechanism.

papers.title: Apigenin Attenuates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Endothelial Activation and Injury-Associated Phenotypes in Human Umbilical Vein Endothelial Cells.
papers.abstract: Sepsis represents a severe challenge in critical‑care medicine. Protecting endothelial function and alleviating microvascular inflammation and oxidative stress help reduce sepsis‑associated mortality. Apigenin, a natural flavonoid, exerts anti‑inflammatory and anti‑oxidant effects; its mechanisms against endothelial injury relevant to sepsis remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether apigenin, a natural flavonoid, can protect human umbilical vein endothelial cells from lipopolysaccharide-induced activation and injury, a model relevant to sepsis-associated endothelial dysfunction. The abstract indicates the work examines anti-inflammatory and antioxidant mechanisms, though specific quantitative findings are not provided in the excerpt. It aims to clarify apigenin's protective mechanisms against endothelial injury in the context of sepsis.

papers.title: Enhancing the flexibility of the peripheral regions within the catalytic cavity of a family 5 glycoside hydrolase CelB for improving catalytic efficiency.
papers.abstract: Glycoside Hydrolase family 5 (GH5) endoglucanases are indispensable biocatalysts in lignocellulosic biorefining and their intrinsic catalytic performances play vital roles in process economics and enable broader industrial applicability. Herein, we engineered the catalytic domain of a bi-modular GH5 endoglucanase CelB from Bacillus sp. Strain N-4 by targeting non-conserved residues around peripheral, solvent-exposed regions. The site-specific mutagenesis identified two single-point mutants Y40G and T177N, which exhibited 1.64- and 1.55-fold increases in specific activity, respectively. Molecul
papers.summary: The authors engineered a GH5 endoglucanase (CelB) by mutating non-conserved residues in the peripheral, solvent-exposed regions of its catalytic cavity. Two single mutants (Y40G and T177N) showed 1.55–1.64-fold increases in specific activity, suggesting that increasing flexibility at the cavity periphery can improve catalytic efficiency. This offers a targeted protein-engineering strategy for improving industrial cellulases.

papers.title: Clinical characterization and in silico structural analysis of microtubule-related gene variants in eleven patients.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to analyze associations of Microtubules (MTs) mutations with nervous system phenotypes, summarize mutation characteristics of genes including TUBA1A, TUBB2A, TUBB4A, and TUBGCP6, explore clinical phenotypic diversity and molecular mechanisms, and expand the MTs genotype-phenotype spectrum.
papers.summary: This study characterizes microtubule-related gene variants (TUBA1A, TUBB2A, TUBB4A, TUBGCP6) in eleven patients with nervous system phenotypes, combining clinical description with in silico structural modeling to explore genotype-phenotype relationships. The work expands the known mutational and phenotypic spectrum of microtubule-related disorders and offers structural hypotheses for how these variants may disrupt protein function.

papers.title: Microcystin-LR exposure induces cartilage degeneration and dysregulates osteoarthritis-associated targets: an integrative computational and experimental study.
papers.abstract: Microcystin-LR (MC-LR), a prevalent cyanotoxin in eutrophic freshwater, is becoming a more widespread environmental contaminant as global warming promotes cyanobacterial blooms, and its health effects may extend beyond its well-documented hepatotoxicity.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether microcystin-LR, a common cyanobacterial toxin, can damage cartilage and contribute to osteoarthritis. Using an integrative approach that combines computational target prediction with experimental validation, the authors show that MC-LR exposure induces cartilage degeneration and dysregulates genes and pathways associated with osteoarthritis.

papers.title: Olanzapine induces Mdivi-1-resistant disruption of insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells.
papers.abstract: Second-generation antipsychotics such as olanzapine (OLZ) are widely prescribed because they produce fewer extrapyramidal adverse effects than first-generation agents. However, OLZ is strongly associated with metabolic dysfunction, and alterations in mitochondrial dynamics have been proposed to contribute to these effects. We investigated whether OLZ-induced mitochondrial dysfunction is linked to impaired insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells and explored a potential interaction with the mitochondrial fission regulator dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1).
papers.summary: This study shows that the antipsychotic drug olanzapine disrupts insulin signaling in skeletal muscle cells through a mechanism that involves mitochondrial dysfunction but cannot be rescued by Mdivi-1, an inhibitor of the mitochondrial fission protein DRP1. The findings suggest that olanzapine's metabolic side effects may involve DRP1-independent pathways, complicating potential therapeutic strategies targeting mitochondrial dynamics.

papers.title: Integrated bulk and single-cell transcriptomic analyses suggest a myeloid-associated candidate role of THBS1 in sepsis.
papers.abstract: Sepsis remains a major cause of mortality worldwide, and biomarkers that integrate inflammatory dysregulation, immune-cell localization, and prognostic relevance remain limited. To identify a candidate molecule linked to myeloid immune responses in sepsis, we performed an integrated analysis of public bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing data, a small exploratory clinical RNA-sequencing cohort, and compound screening analyses.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data from public datasets and a small clinical cohort to identify THBS1 as a candidate biomarker linked to myeloid immune responses in sepsis. Compound screening analyses further suggest THBS1 as a potential therapeutic target. The findings are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts.

papers.title: Novel compound heterozygous mutations of DOCK2 associated with early-onset recurrent infections.
papers.abstract: Dedicator of cytokinesis 2 (DOCK2) deficiency is a rare combined immunodeficiency characterized by defects in both cellular and humoral immunity and caused by pathogenic mutations in the DOCK2 gene. Herein, we report a 3-year-8-month-old Chinese girl presenting with recurrent infections, immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), elevated IgE levels, and a hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH)-like episode to broaden the clinical phenotype spectrum of the DOCK2 defect.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 3-year-8-month-old Chinese girl with a rare combined immunodeficiency caused by novel compound heterozygous mutations in DOCK2. Her presentation included recurrent infections, immune thrombocytopenia, elevated IgE, and an HLH-like episode, expanding the known clinical spectrum of DOCK2 deficiency.
